art.subject: Golden-crowned Sparrow (Zonotrichia atricapilla), adult in spring (breeding) plumage, a vagrant in Korea in April: a broad black cap covering the sides of the crown, with a golden-yellow patch on the forecrown that fades to pale grey on the rear crown; face, throat and breast plain grey; belly whitish; flanks warm buff-brown; mantle brown with dark streaks; wings brown with two white wing bars; tail long and plain brown. Bill dusky grey above, paler below; eye dark; legs pinkish.
art.pose: foraging on the ground beside a thicket, side view
art.scene: thicket edge and grassy field margin in Korea in early spring (April), fresh green buds, soft light; no people, buildings or text
art.build: A large, long-tailed American sparrow, clearly larger than a House Sparrow, plump with a rounded crown; feeds on the ground near cover with an upright stance. Bill conical, rather small, shorter than the head. Legs pinkish, medium length. The long tail extends well beyond the wingtips; tail plain brown with no white.
avoid: Do not paint white crown stripes or a white supercilium — that is White-crowned Sparrow.
Do not paint a pink or orange bill; Golden-crowned Sparrow's bill is dusky grey.
Do not paint yellow on the face or underparts; the yellow is confined to the forecrown.
Do not streak the grey breast.
